deep.reconstruction:
Context from the previous page: a pair (𝒳, 𝒳₀) is equivalent to gluing data (𝒳₀, 𝒳₁, φ), with φ : 𝒳₀ → 𝒳₁ a functor (written φ = f*) that commutes with arbitrary projective limits and is accessible, so it has an adjoint. This is Artin–SGA4 recollement, generalised by dropping left exactness of f*. The question is under what conditions on the data the two inclusions 𝒳₀ → 𝒳 ← 𝒳₁ are weak equivalences.

This page specialises to the case the previous page calls particularly important: 𝒳 = Top(X) with X in (Cat). Equivalently, 𝒳₀ = Top(X₀) and 𝒳₁ = Top(X₁) are presheaf topoi X₀^, X₁^ on small categories. (Grothendieck first wrote X̂₀, X̂₁ and corrected it to Top(X₀), Top(X₁).)

The key observation: a limit-preserving accessible functor between presheaf categories is the 'analogue of f*'. It is determined by a functor X₁ → X₀^. This extends 'by continuity', i.e. by commuting with inductive limits (left Kan extension along the Yoneda embedding), to a cocontinuous functor X₁^ → X₀^, which he labels f* even though it plays the role of the adjoint. Such data is the same as a bifunctor h : X₀^op × X₁ → (Ens), (x₀, x₁) ↦ h(x₁, x₀).

In modern terms this is a profunctor/distributor between X₁ and X₀. The original limit-preserving functor is recovered as φ(F)(x₁) = Hom_{X₀^}(h(x₁, –), F).

What the setup is heading toward: gluing presheaf topoi along φ gives the presheaf category on the collage (cograph) category of h. Its objects are X₀ ⊔ X₁, the original homs within each part, and h(x₁, x₀) as the hom-sets between the two parts. So the 'mapping cylinder' of a distributor is again a small category X with 𝒳 = Top(X). The question 'are X₀ → X ← X₁ weak equivalences' then becomes a Quillen Theorem A question. The inclusion X₁ → X is a weak equivalence iff each presheaf h(–, x₀) on X₁ is aspherical (its category of elements is weakly contractible); dually, X₀ → X is one iff each h(x₁, –) is aspherical. The next page (comma categories A_{/b}, comparison of lim over A_{/b} versus A₁) is visibly starting this cofinality/Theorem-A-type analysis.

When h comes from a functor u : X₁ → X₀, the collage is the categorical mapping cylinder of u. The general case is the cylinder of a correspondence, hence the cote title 'Mapping-cône'.
errors: Directional sloppiness: on the previous page φ = f* goes 𝒳₀ → 𝒳₁ and commutes with limits. Here the cocontinuous extension X₁^ → X₀^ is also labelled f*, though it is really the (left) adjoint of the limit-preserving φ. Grothendieck hedges this by calling it 'un analogue à f*'.

The machine transcription renders the second 'lim' (the 'by continuity' extension) as a projective limit. Mathematically the extension X₁ → X₀^ ⇒ X₁^ → X₀^ must be by inductive limits (colimits); the image appears to show an underlined lim with a rightward arrow there.

ideas.what: Limit-preserving accessible functors between presheaf topoi correspond to functors X₁ → X₀^, i.e. to bifunctors X₀^op × X₁ → Ens.
ideas.modern_name: Profunctors/distributors; Yoneda/Kan-extension classification of cocontinuous functors between presheaf categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bénabou (distributeurs, 1967/1973), Lawvere; also SGA4 Exp. I for extension of functors to presheaves
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. I (extension to presheaf categories); the explicit bifunctor viewpoint is unsure

ideas.what: Gluing of (not necessarily left-exact) data along φ, specialised to presheaf topoi; the glued category is presheaves on the collage of the profunctor h, viewed as a mapping cylinder.
ideas.modern_name: Artin gluing / recollement; collage (cograph) of a profunctor; categorical mapping cylinder
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin (SGA4 Exp. IV §9.5) for gluing; collage folklore (Street, Bénabou); mapping cylinder of categories (Thomason, Cisinski)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 IV 9.5 for topos gluing; cylinder ideas appear in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs (unsure of exact form)

ideas.what: Asking when the inclusions 𝒳₀ → 𝒳 ← 𝒳₁ into the glued object are weak equivalences.
ideas.modern_name: Quillen Theorem A for collages: a profunctor whose representable fibers are aspherical gives a weak equivalence (a 'homotopy-equivalence correspondence')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (Theorem A, 1973); asphericity theory: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks), Maltsiniotis, Cisinski
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses asphericity and Theorem A; the profunctor/cylinder version is unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a homotopy theory of correspondences (distributors) between small categories via the glued presheaf topos / collage, aiming for asphericity conditions under which both inclusions are weak equivalences. This is a profunctor version of the mapping cylinder in his asphericity framework. The criterion (fiberwise asphericity of h(–, x₀) and h(x₁, –)) is well within reach but is not stated on this page.
missed.quote: correspondant à un bifoncteur (x₀, x₁) ↦ h(x₁, x₀), X₀^op × X₁ → (Ens)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Correspondences inducing weak equivalences between categories appear in later work (e.g. Lurie's correspondences, Cisinski's homotopy theory of small categories), but are rarely attributed to Grothendieck. It shows he was treating profunctors as morphisms in the homotopy theory of Cat around 1981. The result itself is folklore, though.

deep.surprise_reason: The page only sets up the standard equivalence between limit-preserving functors of presheaf categories and profunctors, in a recollement / mapping-cylinder context. Mildly interesting as evidence of Grothendieck using distributors in homotopy theory, but the content is classical.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 is more likely 'que φ commute aux lim (projective) quelconques, i.e. ...'; 'quelconque [?]' is a misreading of 'φ commute'.
The second limit ('par "continuité" via lim') should be an inductive limit (varinjlim / colimit), not varprojlim.
Line 3 is plausibly '... un adjoint à g. [à gauche] f*, qui est bien défini par une fonction [foncteur]', i.e. the left-adjoint analogue of f*.
'par une fonction' is likely 'par un foncteur'.
